findings: replicated base average cSDR 7.42 versus original 8.24
small-model variability about 0.3 dB vocals and 0.1 dB average

source_cards.title: The Internet Archive Music Dataset
source_cards.finding: A very large captioned full-mix catalogue can support rights-aware discovery, but per-sample licences, uploader uncertainty, heuristic copyright screening and machine captions prevent automatic reference or training approval.
limitations: uploader-declared licence metadata may be wrong
captions are machine generated and not human verified
lossy full mixes rather than raw stems
caption study is not a production-quality study

findings: repository maps to arXiv 2603.09187 and includes optimized variants absent from the short paper
fast cSDR differs from museval because of silent-frame NaN handling
seed 42 is configured while deterministic execution is disabled
missing checkpoints may initialise random weights
no automated sum-consistency, leakage, true-peak, loudness, phase/mono, boundary, latency or tail tests found

implementation_audits.licence: MIT for authored code; per-sample Creative Commons for audio
findings: repository reports 4.25M clips versus about 4.1M in the paper
per-sample licence and provenance fields exist
ND material is excluded because audio is re-encoded
third-party evaluation code and models retain separate licences
dataset contains full mixes, not multitrack stems

dataset_cards.reason: mixed per-file licences, uploader-rights uncertainty, machine captions and full-mix MP3 scope

knowledge_cards.claim: Same-author retitled arXiv submissions with one repository and overlapping experiments form one version family, not independent confirmation.
A replication gap must be reported against an exact metric implementation, split, checkpoint and configuration.
SDR or cSDR improvement does not establish better downstream mixing or listener preference.
Small single-seed deltas are weak evidence when they are comparable to observed seed variance.
Longer STFT windows can trade temporal precision for frequency resolution; the effect is source and model specific.
Energy claims require hardware, stopping rule, failed-run accounting and quality target.
Missing-checkpoint fallback to random weights is a safety failure unless inference stops before rendering.
Separator pseudo-stems require sum-consistency, leakage, boundary, transient, phase/mono and peak tests before mix use.
An uploader-declared Creative Commons field is evidence to inspect, not proof that the uploader controlled every right.
Code licence, dataset licence and per-file audio licence are separate permissions.
Machine captions support discovery but need human verification before genre, role or reference labels become project knowledge.
A catalogue of lossy full mixes is not a multitrack benchmark and cannot support raw-stem DSP measurements.
